messages.subject: Re: CRAN package RPostgreSQL
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kurt Hornik,

Thank you for the comment on the LICENSE.

The line in DESCRIPTION
 License: GPL-2 | file LICENSE
indicates that the whole package can be distributed under pure GPL-2.
By this line, I intended that a user who is satisfied with GPL-2 need not
read the LICENSE file based on the OR connection of the License.

This is why the license line was not
>  License: GPL-2 + file LICENSE


The alternate LICENSE is not to restrict the right of the users but
to allow the files under src/libpq/ be grabbed out of the package 
and used (modified, distributed or whatever) in accordance 
to the PostgreSQL License.  
As you point out, combined work that contain both GPL-2 
licensed parts and PostgreSQL licensed parts as a whole 
automatically must be licensed under GPL-2 if distributed.

> and modify the first sentence in file LICENSE as
> needed.


If the current sentence is confusing perhaps we can add a note that
the whole package is licensed under GPL-2 and a specific part can be
excised under different terms.

What do you think if we modify the first paragraph as follows:

Most of this package are distributed under GPL-2 (GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE
version 2) with the exception for files under src/libpq/.
While the whole package containing both parts is licensed under GPL-2 you may
use the files under src/libpq in accordance with the PostgreSQL License if separated
from other parts.

See the file COPYING in the top level of the R directory tree for further details of GPL-2.

Sincerely,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan


On 2012/06/11, at 15:19, Kurt Hornik wrote:

> Dear maintainer,
> 
> You have
> 
>  Most of this package are distributed under GPL-2 (GNU GENERAL PUBLIC
>  LICENSE version 2) with the exception for files under src/libpq/ and
>  libpq.dll.
> 
> in your LICENSE file, which apparently is confusing to users.
> 
> You cannot really mix GPL-2 with another license in one package: either
> the other license is *compatible with GPL*, in which case everything is
> available under GPL, or it is not, in which case there is no valid
> license for the package.
> 
> In your case, the PostgreSQL License seems to be a variant of 3-clause
> BSD, so it should be compatible with GPL.  If so, I guess you should
> change to
> 
>  License: GPL-2 + file LICENSE
> 
> in your DESCRIPTION, and modify the first sentence in file LICENSE as
> needed.
> 
> Best
> -k

messages.subject: Re: CRAN package RPostgreSQL
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kurt,

> My understanding is that the PostgreSQL License requires attribution,
> which is compatible with GPL.  But using just GPL-2 as one alternative
> in the license spec would typically be taken to mean that only the base
> GPL license terms apply, which I don't think is the case here. 

Compatible with GPL means that there is no restriction other than GPL and
the combined derivative work may be released under GPL without additional terms.
The request to keep the copyright notice is defined in term 1 of GPL-2 
in other wording. Thus, applying only GPL-2 terms is sufficient. Moreover,
the term 2b requests that the whole package must be licensed under the
term of GPL-2.  

The LICENSE file is intended to tell that GPL-2 need not applied a specific part
but the PostgreSQL License applies to the specific part, (if GPL-2 part is 
totally removed).  This condition is important for easy feedback to
PostgreSQL project.  At the same time, we need to explain the lincense of other part,
i.e. the most part is covered with GPL-2.

Everything under PostgreSQL is not an option as the codebase we started contain
GPLed codes.

Best regards,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL memory allocation error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wytze,

Thank you for reporting the problem.
It is generally difficult to solve any problem that takes
days to reproduce.
Is getStringRelations(), called very large number of times?
If so, making connection outside the function and pass to the
function could be better as not making much number of connections.

If the above reduces the failure as well, perhaps,
making a simpler test programs, (1) just connect, disconnect many times,
(2) connect, dbGetQeury, and disconnect many times will narrow
the problem.

Could you also please test the latest svn version of RPostgreSQL?
the r230 was applied due to strange code but without finding
real evidence of harm in the older code.  If this solved any problem,
we will make it release soon. 
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan
